subtheme: Regulated rate-base growth and utility buildout
claim_statement: Load growth is becoming regulated capital deployment through capital plans, rate-base growth, service agreements, transmission opportunity, turbines, and recovery mechanisms.
what_is_proven: Company disclosures support large capital plans, rate-base or capital-employed growth, signed or secured load/service agreements, turbine procurement, recovery mechanisms, and transmission opportunities.
what_is_not_proven: They do not yet prove project-by-project regulatory approval, customer-specific economics, realized allowed returns, or that every load request becomes profitable rate base.
next_disproof_test: Pick AEP and Duke load queues and reconcile signed, expected, secured, late-stage, and in-service MW by quarter; flag cancellations or delayed interconnection.
next_primary_source_step: Extract exact annual/quarterly report tables for capex by segment, rate-base by utility, load queue definitions, approved projects, recovery riders, and customer contribution language.

claim_statement: Power scarcity is monetized through generation scale, PPAs, fleet availability, customer-backed power projects, and acquisitions of dispatchable capacity.
what_is_proven: Official releases, decks, and filings support contracted MW, generation fleet scale, availability, adjusted EBITDA, BYOP project framing, and generation acquisition scale.
what_is_not_proven: They do not yet prove PPA prices, duration economics, counterparty credit quality, fuel-cost pass-through, financing stack, or customer versus ratepayer cost allocation.
next_disproof_test: For NRG BYOP and Constellation/CyrusOne, test whether disclosed documents show who funds capacity, who bears fuel/interconnection risk, and whether existing customers are insulated.
next_primary_source_step: Extract PPA/BYOP references from 10-Qs, 8-K exhibits, management discussion, project approvals, and investor deck footnotes.

claim_statement: Energy-demand growth is also pulling capital into gathering, processing, fractionation, transportation, storage, refined-products, crude, and export systems.
current_strength: Strong for capex and volume direction; weaker for project economics
what_is_proven: Official packages support capex guidance, EBITDA guidance, NGL/export/Permian volume strength, debt scale, liquidity, and integrated logistics language.
what_is_not_proven: They do not yet separate maintenance capex from growth capex in enough detail, prove individual project returns, or isolate fee-based earnings from commodity/marketing exposure.
next_disproof_test: Compare capex guidance to project lists and volume changes; reject the claim where growth capex is not tied to named capacity additions or durable volume commitments.
next_primary_source_step: Extract project-level schedules, capex categories, volume tables, fee-based percentage, leverage, maturities, and acquisition-integration bridges from 10-Qs and supplements.

claim_statement: Capital only becomes infrastructure when contractors convert awards and backlog into miles, GW, sites, systems, revenue, EBITDA, and cash.
evidence_level: Level 3 official-source proof with execution-risk caveat
what_is_proven: Official sources support backlog, book-to-bill, committed-and-awarded projects, physical output, power transmission miles, telecom miles, renewable GW installed, natural-gas generation awards, revenue growth, and operating cash flow.
what_is_not_proven: They do not prove that every backlog dollar is high-margin, executable on time, or convertible into free cash flow; Primoris is the current caution case.
next_disproof_test: Track backlog conversion against revenue, EBITDA margin, operating cash flow, and project charges for each contractor over the next four quarters.
next_primary_source_step: Extract segment backlog, backlog aging, customer concentration, gross margin, working capital, project reserves, claims, and cash conversion from 10-Qs and annual reports.

claim_statement: The AI/data-center story should be tested beyond utilities and generators by following the physical and service adjacencies: fiber, cabling, building systems, facilities, security, and mission-critical operations.
evidence_rows: TEP-005; TEP-007; queued from lane candidate logic
companies: ABM; CACI; Dycom; MasTec; selected service peers
what_is_proven: The existing power/grid work already shows data-center demand touching utilities, power projects, fiber, and building systems.
what_is_not_proven: It does not yet show a full source-backed chain from hyperscaler capex to service-provider revenue, labor demand, facility operations, or defense/secure-infrastructure adjacency.
next_disproof_test: If ABM/CACI packets do not disclose data-center, mission-critical, secure-facility, or infrastructure-service metrics, keep them as adjacent context rather than a core power/grid claim.
next_primary_source_step: Run source-upgrade packets for ABM, CACI, and other high-score digital-infrastructure adjacency companies; extract annual-report revenue lines and backlog/service contract references.

claim_statement: The defensible big-picture claim is that power/grid is a capital-absorption lane: money is moving into capacity and constraints across generation, wires, fuel logistics, and field execution.
companies: Constellation; NextEra; Duke; AEP; Exelon; Vistra; NRG; ONEOK; Targa; MasTec; Dycom; Primoris; Granite
evidence_level: Level 3 company-source proof; not yet Level 5 outside-denominator proof
current_strength: Good enough for a bounded thesis; not enough for a market-wide conclusion
what_is_proven: The evidence proves a multi-layer company disclosure pattern: contracted MW, service agreements, capital plans, rate-base metrics, generation acquisitions, availability, customer-backed power, midstream capex, volume growth, backlog, book-to-bill, CAP, physical output, and cash-flow/EBITDA bridges.
what_is_not_proven: It does not prove that AI explains all power investment, that all investments earn attractive returns, that capital access is unlimited, or that customer/ratepayer affordability questions are solved.
next_disproof_test: Try to disprove the system claim with non-AI demand drivers, regulatory rejection, interconnection delays, fuel constraints, contractor margin pressure, or backlog that does not convert into cash.
next_primary_source_step: Add outside denominators: EIA capacity, FERC transmission, ISO interconnection queues, utility rate cases, state commission orders, bank/project-finance data, and quarterly capex time series.
